title: EBS volumes, instance store and EFS

videos.script: An instance has disks, and they do not all behave alike. This lesson is about which disk to give it. {{volumes}} Most of the time the answer is an EBS volume. It is a disk on the network, and you choose three numbers for it: its size, its operations per second, and its throughput. You will price each one with AWS's own figures. {{zone}} A volume lives in one zone. It attaches only to instances in that zone, and it outlives them when you ask it to. You will see what a termination deletes, and what it leaves behind, still billed. {{store}} Then the disk inside the host. Instance store is fast and already paid for. It is also gone the moment the instance stops. {{efs}} And last, a file system that many instances share at once, across every zone. EFS costs more per gigabyte, and you only pay for what you store. By the end you can say, for any data, where it should live, and what it costs a month to keep it there.
